How to Apply for French School Scholarships in Boston for 2026-2027
Families newly arrived in the Boston consular district must submit their applications for the 2026-2027 school year scholarship program by September 25, 2026. This secondary campaign, managed by the Consulate General of France, provides financial assistance for French children attending schools homologated by the French Ministry of National Education.
Eligibility Requirements for Scholarship Applicants
To qualify for the scholarship program, students and their families must meet specific criteria established by the Agency for French Education Abroad (AEFE). According to the official guidance from the French diplomatic mission in the United States, applicants must be registered with the Register of French Nationals Established Outside of France. The student must hold French nationality, be at least three years old by December 31, 2026, and reside with a parent or legal guardian within the Boston consular district, which encompasses Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Maine, and Vermont.
Financial assistance is contingent upon the family’s socioeconomic situation and the cost of tuition. Importantly, the scholarship program is distinct from the school admission process. Securing a grant does not guarantee a spot at an institution, and families are advised to coordinate with their chosen school’s admissions office independently. Parents currently employed as public-sector agents abroad are ineligible for this specific aid, and families must provide a certificate of termination of benefits from the French Family Allowance Fund (CAF) if they previously resided in France.
Homologated Institutions in New England
The scholarship program exclusively supports students enrolled in schools recognized by the French government. In the New England region, these institutions include the International School of Boston, the Ecole Française Boston, the French American School of Rhode Island, and the Ecole Française du Maine. These schools are required to follow the curriculum and pedagogical standards mandated by the French Ministry of National Education.
Navigating the complexities of international enrollment often requires professional support.
The Scholarship Timeline and Application Process
The 2026-2027 academic year scholarship cycle operates on a strict schedule. While the primary campaign concluded in February 2026, the current secondary campaign is reserved for families who arrived in the region after the initial deadline or those seeking a revision of a previously notified decision. According to the Consulate General of France in Boston, dossiers must be complete and submitted with all required supporting documentation by the September 25 deadline. Any applications received after this date are subject to automatic rejection.
Following the submission, the Consular Scholarship Council meets in early November to review these specific cases. Final decisions are then referred to the National Scholarship Commission in Paris, with families expected to be notified of the outcome by the end of December. This process is designed to accommodate the realities of international mobility, yet it remains a rigid administrative procedure.
The scholarship program is designed to alleviate the financial burden of tuition fees for French families abroad, but it requires adherence to specific institutional reporting and documented residency requirements, according to the official guidance on school aid.
Managing Financial and Legal Transitions
The transition to a new educational system involves significant logistical planning. Beyond the scholarship application, families must often address broader legal or financial requirements associated with their move to the United States.
Failure to provide a comprehensive and verified dossier is the most common reason for application delays or denials in this highly regulated funding environment.
The path forward requires careful preparation.
